title: The Room Keeps Its Own
prompt: He wanted the count raised. He wrote this. The count did not move. One last time — find the line.

config.symptom: it prints 10. The spell ran, returned the right answer, and nothing changed.

line_hints.2: The spell takes what it needs. Nothing wrong with asking for it.
line_hints.3: Inside the room this is right — n really does become 11.
line_hints.4: And it hands 11 back, faithfully. The spell does its whole job.
line_hints.7: Printing only shows what survived. It is telling the truth.

fixes.why: There it is. The spell was handing 11 back and nobody was catching it. A return is an offer — you must accept it by name.
That would work, but it makes the spell reach out and change the world behind your back. A function that returns a value and is caught is the cleaner magic.
You would SEE 11 — and count would still be 10 the moment after. Showing a value is not keeping it.

config.success: The room keeps its own. What happens inside stays inside — unless you catch what it hands you.
